interface_notes.value: The coarse-grained polycrystalline as-cast Fe-15%Al alloy contains grain boundaries (grain size ~1 mm) but no second phases or precipitates at the boundaries in the as-cast condition. Thin carbide precipitates on grain boundaries appeared only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged annealing (e.g. 14 days at 320 °C), and were rare/tiny for low-C (20 wt.ppm) alloys - the regime of this composition - under those heat treatments; none are present in the as-cast state.

unmapped_findings: Composition of this sample (Table 1, nominal 15 at.% Al row): real Al content 14.9 at.% (7.8 wt.-%); impurities C = 20 wt.ppm, Si = 60 wt.ppm, Ni < 40 wt.ppm. (No composition field exists in the schema; the alloy snapshot gives 14.9 at.% / 7.8 wt.-% and C 20, Si 60, Ni<40.)

The polycrystalline as-cast Fe-15%Al belongs to the polycrystalline series (4-18 at.% Al) that shows a coarse grain structure (grain size of the order of 1 mm) and no second phases in the as-cast condition.

Solid-solution hardening (series-level, includes this composition): the compressive yield stress of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.%; the interpolating straight lines indicate a yield stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit% for the higher (10^-2 s^-1) and lower (10^-4 s^-1) compression rates, respectively, and a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa (Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys). No individual numeric value is reported for the 15 at.% composition.

At -100 °C, deformation twinning occurred for Al contents above 14 at.% in all specimens (this range includes Fe-15%Al); at room temperature deformation twinning was observed only for the Fe-18%Al alloy.

Ductility (series-level): the strain before necking and fracture strain decrease with increasing Al content; ductile fracture with necking holds up to about 15 at.% Al at room temperature and about 12 at.% Al at -100 °C, with a transition to brittle fracture without necking in the range 15-18 at.% Al at room temperature and 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C. This 15 at.% Al composition lies at the onset of the room-temperature ductile-to-brittle transition.
The tension-test results are averages of 3-4 tests and the yield stress/strength data differed by 3% at most; compression tests typically used two specimens per alloy which differed by 3% at most.
